new_findings_today.title: Uttarkashi SOS publishes a literal placeholder phone `+91-94120-XXXXX` for `Taxi Union Uttarkashi`
new_findings_today.detail: /en/destination/uttarkashi page contains `"phone":"+91-94120-XXXXX"` in the embedded RSC payload for the Taxi Union Uttarkashi SOS contact. The `XXXXX` substring is a literal redacted-template placeholder, not a real phone number. This violates the CLAUDE.md rule: "All data must be real and verifiable — zero fabricated phones, contacts, statistics. Honest scarcity (`[]`) preferred over fabrication." The other 4 Uttarkashi phones (+91-1374-222123, 01352559898, 1070, 112) are valid Indian formats. Across the 10-destination sample, this is the only invalid phone (1 / 27 = 3.7%).
new_findings_today.evidence: section-E-sos.csv — uttarkashi row: 5 phones extracted, 1 invalid_format = `+9194120XXXXX`. Source HTML context: `"name":"Taxi Union Uttarkashi","role":"Taxi stand with 24/7 service to Rishikesh/Gangotri","phone":"+91-94120-XXXXX"` (RSC payload).
new_findings_today.recommendation: Either (a) replace `+91-94120-XXXXX` with the actual Taxi Union Uttarkashi number sourced from a verifiable channel (district tourism office, taxi stand signage, news reference), or (b) drop the contact entirely and let the Taxi Union row fall to honest-scarcity null. Then audit the rest of the 488-destination corpus for any other `XXXXX`/`XXXX`/`####` placeholder strings in `phone` fields — `grep -roE '"phone":"[^"]*X{2,}[^"]*"' supabase/seed*.sql data/sos/` and `grep -roE '"phone":"[^"]*#{2,}[^"]*"'` should surface any siblings.

new_findings_today.title: Self-corrected false-negative on hreflang grep: site uses `hrefLang` (camelCase JSX), not `hreflang`
new_findings_today.detail: First Section-D run with case-sensitive `grep -E 'hreflang="en"'` returned 0/12 — would have shown a regression vs. yesterday's 12/12. Investigation showed the head emits `<link rel="alternate" hrefLang="en" ...>` (React JSX preserves casing). Re-ran with `grep -i` and got the expected 12/12. Documenting so future probes use case-insensitive matching, and noting this matches the existing memory entry `nakshiq_hreflang_fix.md` (next-intl 4.9 emits broken x-default, so Next.js metadata is the single hreflang source, and React renders it camelCased).
new_findings_today.evidence: section-D-seo.csv (final, case-insensitive); 12/12 canonical, 12/12 hreflang en/hi/x-default, 12/12 og:image, 0/12 title stutter.
new_findings_today.recommendation: Bake `grep -i` into qa/SKILL.md guidance for SEO meta probes. No code change required.
